title: ArcCivs 0.1.44: Creative requested-supply parity for building and resident menus
assumptions: Before 0.1.43 an explicit non-tool request requires a plain existing player storage item even in Creative, while profession-tool requests and construction grants already support Creative issuance. After, a city manager in Creative may fulfil only a current ordinary material request through either existing menu, using the same durable inventory receipt.

An accepted click creates at most min(current shortage, native material maxStackSize, actual destination room). TORCH and LADDER have maxStackSize64. A satisfied, busy, invalid or full request issues zero. Existing tools remain one. This is Creative testing capability, not normal-player income; native Creative item creation already exists.

Survival, including operators in Survival, still transfers exact existing native items; no source debit is bypassed there. City access, proximity, request validity, native metadata and once-only durable commits remain. Removing issued items then repeating can issue more, as existing Creative construction grants can; no lifetime issuance limit is claimed.

Sensitivity assumptions only: 1/2/4 Creative city managers, 0.25/1/2 active hours per day and 4/4/6 accepted explicit requests per hour, hence1/4/12 requests per manager-day. An illustrative fitting torch or ladder request supplies8/32/64 items respectively. These are separate mutually exclusive scenarios, not telemetry, guarantees or imposed daily limits.

Native items may be moved and eventually sold via current SELL, trade or contracts; no material redemption price or currency conversion is invented. The future SELL-to-contract transition is not assumed active. No progression purchase or price changes; days-to-save is inapplicable to free native Creative issuance.

Correcting mine shaft routing and shelter reservations may restore useful travel and production but adds no synthetic harvest, per-action profession reward, work-duration change or offline catch-up. Each recovered previously missed mine wall or light consumes zero before and one cobblestone or one torch after, respectively; unit repair cost is unchanged. Frequency and total restored repair consumption are not measured. Disconnected cave walls are deferred until real excavation opens their frontier, without charging again for committed repairs. Realized throughput and resulting indirect sale income are not measured.
Direct Vault, tokens and player XP remain separately0→0. Source tests, exact delivered artifact, active runtime and real protocol/native-client observations are separate evidence layers.

flows.source: CivsUi building/NPC request -> CivsService -> CivsStorage durable receipt
flows.basis: Incremental plain torch or ladder units for Creative manager with empty source inventory; separate scenarios, no monetary valuation.
